title: Benchmarking 3D and 2.5D Convolutional and Transformer Architectures for Ovarian Tumour Classification on Clinical CT with Quantified Cross-Architecture Explanation Agreement
content: Post-hoc explanation methods are routinely reported alongside deep learning models for 2 medical imaging, yet whether architecturally distinct models attend to the same anatomy 3 when classifying the same scan is rarely examined. We address this question on a clinical 4 computed tomography cohort of 190 contrast-enhanced volumes from 165 patients acquired 5 through NHS Scotland, benchmarking fifteen architectures spanning three-dimensional 6 volumetric and 2.5D slice-based families under a common protocol with patient-level 7 stratified group cross-validation. Spatial overlap between Gradient-weighted Class Activa- 8 tion Mapping and Attention Rollout is then measured by an Intersection over Union on 9 percentile-thresholded maps, for which the chance level is analytically determined. Vision 10 Transformer Base/16 achieved the highest discrimination at an area under the curve of 11 0.896, while volumetric models ranked higher on accuracy than on discrimination. Substi- 12 tuting RadImageNet for ImageNet cost 4.7 and 24.2 percentage points of accuracy where 13 matched weights allowed a controlled comparison, a penalty comparable to the spread 14 across architectures. Mean explanation agreement was 0.336, three times the chance level 15 of 0.111, but 12.6% of volumes fell at or below chance and agreement proved decoupled 16 from predictive correctness. These results indicate that explanation agreement should not 17 be treated as a proxy for reliability without prior validation.
